title: Physics-informed retrieval-augmented language model guides synthesis of five previously unreported inorganic crystals
summary: Researchers built PIRAG-LM, which combines a structured knowledge base of experimental synthesis routes, physics-based chemical/structural/thermodynamic similarity retrieval, and LLM route reasoning. In prospective tests, it guided synthesis of five compounds previously unreported in experimental literature: BaMo0.3In0.7O2.95, BaNb0.4In0.6O2.9, Hg[B(CN)4]2, CoCo(CN)6 and SrNb2Fe2(PO4)6. Powder X-ray diffraction patterns were consistent with target phases. This is one paper-level synthesis-planning result, not five separate entries.
ai_technology: PIRAG-LM, physics-informed retrieval-augmented language model, with DeepSeek-V4 used in the structured synthesis-knowledge-base extraction workflow
organization: Soochow University; Zhengzhou University; Fudan University; Hefei National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Researchers built PIRAG-LM, which combines a structured knowledge base of experimental synthesis routes, physics-based chemical/structural/thermodynamic similarity retrieval, and LLM route reasoning.
evidence.unknown: This is a source-checked preprint (not treated as peer-reviewed here). The reported new-compound claims refer to absence from experimental literature and prospective synthesis; PXRD matches support target phase formation, but the paper does not establish broad application performance or independent replication. Experts selected materials and adjusted operational conditions; the system did not autonomously run experiments. Five compounds remain bundled as one paper-level finding.
evidence.ai_role: PIRAG-LM retrieved synthesis precedents by chemical, structural and thermodynamic similarity and proposed synthesis methods, precursors and processing conditions. Experts evaluated routes and refined practical parameters; researchers synthesized and characterized the five target phases. The final route class, precursor logic and main processing sequence generally followed model recommendations.
